evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep never frames the 10–15 minute time box or promise of a dependable quote, nor waits for customer acknowledgment before diving into details.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after extensive probing: 'Great, and then besides pricing, do you have any questions or concerns you would like answered on this call today?' — came well after Jessica had already detailed the dishwasher flood and storage pod plan.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Rep followed up multiple times: 'and then you said we're gonna go ahead and put it in a pod... what size pod, do you know?' and 'Okay and then are we moving any t.v.s out of there?' and 'and then so we've got the L, sha, couch dishwasher so fridge one bedroom. What size bed is that?' — continued probing on each concern/detail raised.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No summary reflection offered. Rep acknowledged concerns ('Perfect, I can definitely help you out with that') but never synthesized or confirmed: 'So what I'm hearing is...'
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Covered extensively: property type (house, downstairs only), rooms (one bedroom, living room, dining room, half bath), special items (L-shaped couch, entertainment center, appliances—dishwasher, stove, fridge), walking distance was mentioned ('out of our range'), queen bed noted, TV placement discussed.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Never asked. Rep discussed boxes customer would prepare ('I will have boxed up') but did not offer Einstein packing services.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Partial. Rep gave a range ('$670... between $670 and then $878 if we were to hit that $3') but did not anchor it to a typical pod move size or personalize it to this customer's specific situation (insurance claim, appliance moves, two-way moves). Range was presented without context.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Partial. Rep mentioned the $150 trip fee and 2.5-hour minimum ('two and a half hour minimum... time is prorated in 215 minute increments'), but did not frame it as 'not a guess' or address 15-minute increments clearly. Fee transparency incomplete—no mention of deposit or change fees upfront (only mentioned later as reassurance, not proactive disclosure).
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Rep transitioned directly to 'Can you send a quote?' without asking 'Does that feel fair?' and no pause for customer reaction.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Partial. Rep said 'we have the additional $2,000 coverage that included in the hourly rate provides up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for any accidental Andal. Damages' — covers the $2,000 and that it's built into the rate, but did not explicitly state 'no deductible' or 'no fine print' framing. Also introduced 'Meet Your Mover' feature but did not tie it to Two Promises.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No. Rep did not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or any version of closing the loop on the two promises.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Throwaway. Rep asked 'do you have any other questions for me?' — empty, generic phrasing that gets automatic no, not the genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?'
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Not asked. No 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never. Rep never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' Instead, the call ended with Jessica saying 'if you could send that over I will start the process' and rep agreeing to email the quote. Rep accepted the customer's implicit next step (sending quote) without an explicit ask for the business.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Not explicitly. Rep mentioned 'no deposit required to get on the schedule' and 'no charges or fees to change the dates,' which imply flexibility but do not state a rate lock.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Rep confirmed phone number (775-846-9795), email (young1311@gmail.com), and general intent to send quote. Date not confirmed (customer stated date is uncertain pending insurance approval). Arrival window not confirmed. Crew size not confirmed. Return-move address not confirmed. No notes left for crew about customer's concerns (insurance approval delay, driveway difficulty for pod placement).

top_strength: Rep demonstrated strong two-layer probing throughout, consistently asking follow-up questions (appliance types, bed size, TV placement, box quantities) to gather complete move details without losing track of the customer's core constraint: insurance approval pending.
coaching_note: Section 1 must open with the quid pro quo framing (10–15 minutes, dependable quote, wait for yes) before any probing—it sets the call structure; also, Section 7 requires an explicit ask ('Would you like our help?') and booking confirmation with all four details before closing, rather than letting the customer drive next steps.
